target_name: Center for Middle East Peace and Economic Cooperation
summary: The Center's precise legal founding date is January 23, 1989, before Owens's documented March 23-April 1989 bank-promoting mission; the ordering against the Epstein-accompanied 1989 trip remains unresolved.
detail: DC file 890233 gives an effective date of 1989-01-23. On March 9, Owens told the House that he and S. Daniel Abraham had helped organize the Center 'last month.' Contemporaneous reporting dates the separately documented bank mission from March 23 through approximately April 5. Finding #13911 dates the Epstein-accompanied trip only to 1989, so the records establish the Center-before-bank-trip sequence but do not establish Center sponsorship of, or temporal priority over, the exact Epstein-accompanied trip.
source_quote: last month, I helped organize, with prominent New York businessman S. Daniel Abraham, a nonprofit organization, the Center for Middle East Peace and Economic Cooperation

summary: The Center's 990-PF filings report $379,999 compensation to Owens in 2001 and $378,754 in 2002 as president at 40 hours per week.
detail: Part VIII of each return lists Wayne Owens as president, reports 40 hours per week, and gives the compensation amount. The filings verify Center salary but do not characterize the pay as lobbying compensation or allocate it to particular duties.

target_name: Center for Middle East Peace mission program
summary: The Center documented a recurring congressional fact-finding program and publicly named at least five participants in its 1998 mission cycle.
detail: The Center's archived About page claimed more than 40 fact-finding missions since 1989. Its Fall 1998 newsletter named Senator Robert Torricelli and Representatives Gary Ackerman, Tom Campbell, Jim Moran, and David Price and listed travel to Syria, Egypt, Israel, Jordan, Qatar, Lebanon, Gaza, and the West Bank. This is a collective participant list, not a complete trip-by-trip manifest.
source_quote: Participants have included Senator Robert Torricelli, Congressmen Gary Ackerman, Tom Campbell, Jim Moran, and David Price.

summary: Owens died in Tel Aviv on December 18, 2002, immediately after seven days of Center travel with Representatives David Price and Jim Davis.
detail: Price's participant account says the mission met heads of state in Syria, Lebanon, and Israel and held targeted sessions with Omar Suleiman, Abu Mazen, Salam Fayyad, and Sari Nusseibeh. It directly documents the Center's method of small congressional missions, leadership access, and issue briefings.
source_quote: Owens, 64, collapsed and died of a heart attack while walking on a beach in Tel Aviv on Dec. 18.

target_name: Bank for Economic Cooperation and Development in the Middle East and North Africa
summary: The mid-1990s treaty bank is a conceptual descendant of earlier regional-bank advocacy, but reviewed founding sources do not establish Owens/Center legal succession, and the agreement never entered into force.
detail: The UN says negotiations followed a mandate from the October-November 1994 Casablanca summit and currently lists nine signatories, three parties, and the agreement as not yet in force. World Bank material calls the bank an outgrowth of an October 1994 Egypt-Israel-Jordan-PLO proposal. A Cairo transition team performed preparatory work, but the United States did not appropriate its contribution and transition-team funding expired in October 1998. No evidence of lending operations was located. None of the reviewed UN, World Bank, or Kaye records credits Owens or the Center as founder of the treaty bank.
source_quote: NOT YET IN FORCE ... Signatories: 9. Parties: 3.

target_name: Jeffrey Epstein / S. Daniel Abraham Center orbit
summary: A 2014 Rod-Larsen office bulletin sent to Epstein included an Abraham op-ed and Center founder biography, but no Epstein/Wexner institutional role appeared in the reviewed Center layers.
detail: EFTA02720449 is an April 5, 2014 email from the Office of Terje Rod-Larsen to jeevacation@gmail.com. The packet includes an S. Daniel Abraham op-ed and identifies him as founder of the Center. Separately, exact searches across 22 Form 990-PF returns, named archived mission pages, and the reviewed MEDB records produced no Jeffrey Epstein, Leslie Wexner, Michael Yeager, or identified Epstein-vehicle name hit. The email is evidence of content reaching Epstein's inbox, not Center office, funding, mission participation, or direct Abraham-Epstein contact.

target_name: Wayne Owens papers / Center archive disposition
summary: The University of Utah catalog identifies a dedicated Center file and multiple 1988-1989 Middle East trip files and photo folders in the Wayne Owens collections.
detail: MS 0108 catalogs Dan Abraham notes from a 1988 Middle East trip, a 1989 Owens study trip, 1989-1992 trip documents, a 1990-2000 Center file, and separate 1989 Israel and congressional-trip files. P0108 catalogs 1989 Middle East and Egypt-Jordan-Palestine photo folders, a December 2002 last-trip/funeral folder, and circa 1989-1993 group photos. These are catalog references only; the records and images were not reviewed.

target_name: S. Daniel Abraham Center / current status
summary: The Center has conflicting current-status indicators: DC lists the corporation dissolved, while federal, filing, and public-site records show continuing organizational activity.
detail: DC file 890233 was current to July 17, 2026 and lists the domestic nonprofit as dissolved, but exposes neither the dissolution date nor reason in the accessible search record. The IRS BMF still lists EIN 52-1621126 with tax period 2024-12; a 2024 Form 990-PF was filed; and centerpeace.org redirects to a current Center Project site whose schema identifies the S. Daniel Abraham Center for Middle East Peace and names Robert Wexler as president. These records establish a status conflict, not a legal conclusion about authority to operate.
